subject: Woodwork
examFormat: Three papers, all to be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice objective questions in 40 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: theory and design paper in 2 hours 20 minutes; Section A has short structured questions (Part II for Nigeria, Sierra Leone and The Gambia, Part III for all candidates with two questions of which one is answered) and Section B has design and drawing questions, all answered in 1 hour 40 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 3: a practical test of 3 hours making a test piece from supplied drawings, for 100 marks.
excluded: Part I of Paper 2 Section A (Ghana only); recommended tools and machines list and suggested reading list.

topics.name: Practical Work
objectives: Work from dimensioned sketches, written descriptions or working drawings using common hand tools, portable power tools and basic woodworking machines, different joints and shapes, nails, screws and other fasteners and fittings, and solid wood, manufactured boards and non-wood materials
Construct widening joints, e.g. plain/simple butt, dowelled, tongued and grooved, rebated butt
Construct angle joints: box-like construction (e.g. common and lapped dovetail, pin joints) and shelf-like construction (e.g. housing joints, pinned joints, dowelled, plain mitre)
Construct framing joints, e.g. mortise and tenon, bridle and lapped joints, mitre, dowelled
Perform cutting operations, e.g. ripping, cross-cutting
Perform planing operations, e.g. surfacing, thicknessing
Perform shaping operations, e.g. chamfering, rounding and tapering
Assemble and finish, e.g. testing for squareness, parallelism, use of diagonals, trial assembly, cramping methods, preparation of surfaces and application of finishes

topics.name: General Workshop Safety
objectives: State personal safety precautions
State general workshop safety regulations
Identify the types and uses of safety devices and appliances
Observe hand tool safety in carrying, storing and handling hand tools
Observe general machine shop safety, safety precautions in the use of portable power tools and machines, and safety in machine operations
Prevent mechanical faults
Administer first aid (materials and administration)

topics.name: Hand Tools
objectives: Identify, describe and sketch the types of hand tools
Classify hand tools: geometrical, holding and supporting, impelling and percussion, cutting, boring, abrading and scraping tools

topics.name: Special Purpose Hand Tools
objectives: Identify, describe and sketch planes (spokeshaves, rebate plane, plough plane, block plane, shoulder plane etc.) and state their uses
Identify, describe and sketch saws (bow saw, pad/keyhole saw, coping saw, fret saw) and state their uses
Identify, describe and sketch boring bits (expansion bit, forstner bit, countersink bit, auger bit etc.) and state their uses
Identify, describe and sketch shapers (scrapers, rasps, surforms etc.) and state their uses

topics.name: Portable Power Tools
objectives: Identify, describe, care for and safely use portable power tools: power drill, jig saw, spray gun, screw driver, sanders, router, power circular saw etc.
State the uses of portable power tools

topics.name: Woodworking Machines
objectives: Identify, describe, care for and safely use woodworking machines: circular saw, crosscut saw, thicknesser, surface planer, mortiser, lathe, grinding wheel, drilling machine etc.
State the uses of woodworking machines
State safety precautions, including the use of guards, fences, push sticks, push blocks and gauges

topics.name: Maintenance
objectives: Distinguish types of maintenance: corrective, routine, predictive and preventive
State the reasons for maintenance
Maintain hand tools (oiling, sharpening, repairing, storing etc.)
Maintain machines (cleaning, oiling, servicing, replacing parts etc.)

topics.name: West African Timbers in Common Use
objectives: Describe timber growth and structure, including classification (soft/hardwoods) and parts and their functions
Identify common West African timbers, e.g. iroko (odum), abura, mahogany, obeche (wawa), African walnut, afara, ebony, danta, emery, shedua, mansonia, cedar, afromosia (kokrodua), avodire, kusia
State the characteristics of the timbers: surface, working and mechanical qualities, similarities and differences
State the specific uses of the timbers

topics.name: Timber Conversion
objectives: Explain timber conversion
Describe conversion methods: plain/through and through/live sawing, tangential/back/flat/rake sawing, quarter/radial/rift sawing, and their characteristics, advantages and disadvantages
Identify, describe and state the uses of common market sizes: log, plank, scantling, board, batten, strip/lath, squares

topics.name: Timber Seasoning
objectives: Explain timber seasoning and the reasons for it
Describe methods of seasoning: natural/open air, artificial/kiln, water and chemical seasoning, with advantages and disadvantages
Determine moisture content by the moisture meter method and the oven dry method and their advantages and disadvantages
Calculate percentage moisture content

topics.name: Timber Defects
objectives: Explain timber defects
Describe the causes, prevention and remedies of natural growth defects, felling defects, conversion defects, seasoning defects and defects caused by organisms, with description and sketching

topics.name: Timber Preservation
objectives: State the reasons for preserving timber
Identify common timber preservatives and their specific uses
State the properties of a good timber preservative
Describe methods of applying timber preservatives: brushing, dipping, spraying etc., with advantages and disadvantages

topics.name: Manufactured Boards
objectives: Describe the types, structure, characteristics and uses of manufactured boards, with advantages and disadvantages of each type

topics.name: Timber Preparation
objectives: Select tools and machines
Describe the operational sequence: hand preparation and machine preparation
Prepare stock (practical)

topics.name: Woodwork Joints
objectives: Identify, describe, sketch, construct and state the specific use of widening joints: simple butt, dowel, tongued and grooved, loose tongue, rebated butt etc.
Identify, describe, sketch, construct and state the specific use of angle joints: mortise and tenon, dowelled butt, dovetails, housing, halving etc.
Identify, describe, sketch, construct and state the specific use of framing joints: mortise and tenon, bridle, plain mitre, dowelled butt, halving etc.

topics.name: Wood Finishes and Finishing
objectives: Identify types of wood finishes (fillers, stains, paints, varnishes, lacquers, polishes etc.) and state their properties, characteristics and uses
Apply finishes: surface preparation, tools and methods (brushing, spraying, dipping etc.), including the stages and tools for each method
State safety precautions

topics.name: Wood Abrasives
objectives: Explain the meaning of wood abrasives
Identify grades: coarse, medium and fine
Select abrasives and state their uses, including the specific application of each grade

topics.name: Wood Adhesives
objectives: Identify types of adhesives: protein (animal, casein), synthetic resins (urea, phenol and melamine formaldehydes, epoxy resins, polyvinyl acetate (PVA)) and contact/rubber based
State their characteristics, uses, preparation and application, and safety precautions during application

topics.name: Wood Fittings and Fasteners
objectives: Identify, describe, sketch and state the uses, application and fixing of fittings, e.g. hinges, locks, handles, bolts, catches
Identify, describe, sketch and state the uses, application and fixing of fasteners: nails, screws, bolts and nuts, corrugated fasteners etc.

topics.name: Non-wood Materials
objectives: Identify, describe and state the characteristics and uses of non-wood materials: glass, plastics, rubber, ceramics, metal, leather etc.

topics.name: Veneers and Veneering
objectives: Identify, describe and state the types, production and uses of veneers
Describe veneering methods (hammer, press) and the processes for each
Identify, describe, sketch and state the uses of veneering tools: veneer hammer, pressing iron, cramps, caul etc.

topics.name: Wood Shaping and Bending
objectives: Describe shaping: rounding, moulding, bevelling, chamfering, tapering, carving etc.
Describe bending: solid and laminated
Identify, describe and sketch the processes, techniques, tools and machines, and the properties of wood suitable for each

topics.name: Design and Drawing
objectives: Explain the concept of design
Describe design fundamentals and processes
Make free hand sketches
Produce working drawings in first and third angle orthographic projections, with correct sectional representation of the materials
Prepare a cutting list and bill of materials
Apply basic draftsmanship skills

topics.name: Project Design and Construction
objectives: Identify and analyse given design problems arising from customer needs, market survey, situation analysis etc.
Design to solve the problems
Estimate the cost of the design
Construct to meet the design specification
Evaluate the product to meet design purpose and specification

topics.name: Upholstery
objectives: Describe upholstery work, its types and parts
Identify, describe, sketch, care for and use hand tools and machines: needles, pair of scissors, hammer, webbing stretcher, sewing machine, buttoning machine
Identify materials for framing, stuffing/padding, covering and decorating
Describe processes and techniques: framing, padding, covering, finishing, decoration, to be applied in constructing an upholstery project

topics.name: Wood Turning
objectives: Identify, describe, sketch, care for and safely use the wood lathe: parts and accessories
Identify turning tools and their specific use: chisels, gouges, calipers etc.
Describe and carry out turning operations: face plate turning, turning between centres and boring
Identify suitable wood for turning: abura, ebony, mahogany etc.
Produce turning projects: vase, bowl, candle holder etc.

topics.name: Wood Carving and Sculpture
objectives: Describe, identify, apply and carry out the processes of carving: incise and relief
Produce simple ornaments (sculpture)
Identify, sketch and state the uses of tools: chisels, gouges, knives, files etc.

topics.name: Surface Decoration
objectives: Identify, describe and carry out the processes, techniques and application of surface decoration: inlaying, veneering, marquetry, lamination, laminated plastics, mouldings etc.

topics.name: Mass Production
objectives: Explain the concept and principles of mass production, including terms such as templates, fixtures, trial run, departments, section, prototype and quality control
Describe the processes: market survey, design, production, quality assurance, sales/marketing, management, procurement, cost estimation and tooling up for production

topics.name: Entrepreneurship in Woodworking
objectives: Describe types of business organisation, e.g. sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperatives, with characteristics, advantages and disadvantages
Identify business opportunities in woodworking, e.g. merchandizing, spray painting, upholstery work, wood turning
Describe business plans: format and content, including sample plans
Identify sources of funds, e.g. gifts, personal savings, loans, inheritance, cooperatives, with benefits and risks
